MR. BURSCH: Thank you, Mr. Chief
Justice, and may it please the Court:
         This case arises from state officials'
attempt to use state court proceedings to shut
down an international pipeline that supplies
energy to millions in the U.S. and Canada. The
question is whether federal courts retain their
traditional equitable authority to excuse the
30-day removal deadline.  Under this Court's
case law and statutory text, they do.
           To begin, Section 1446(b) is a
non-jurisdictional filing rule, a timing rule,
that satisfies this Court's test in Young
because it prescribes a period within which
certain rights may be enforced.  So, under
Holland, the Court's presumption, it presumes
that federal courts retain their traditional

tolling too.
